title: Dasakam 51 – Aghāsuravadha
description: Krishna leads the cowherd boys and calves into the forest, saves them from Aghasura’s giant serpent form, and shares a joyful meal praised by the gods.
translation_note: No vetted English stanza translation is included. Facebook picture captions are preserved as supplied source commentary at their own #N keys; they are not translations. Canonical Sanskrit and IAST are transcribed from Stotra Nidhi.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदाचन व्रजशिशुभिः समं भवान्
वनाशने विहितमतिः प्रगेतराम् ।
समावृतो बहुतरवत्समण्डलैः
सतेमनैर्निरगमदीश जेमनैः ॥ ५१-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadācana vrajaśiśubhiḥ samaṃ bhavān
vanāśane vihitamatiḥ pragetarām |
samāvṛto bahutaravatsamaṇḍalaiḥ
satemanairniragamadīśa jemanaiḥ || 51-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: One early morning, Krishna wished to go for a picnic to the forest along with the Gopas. They carried eatables, cooked rice and all delicacies and left to the forest with the cows.

stanzas.sanskrit:
विनिर्यतस्तव चरणाम्बुजद्वया-
दुदञ्चितं त्रिभुवनपावनं रजः ।
महर्षयः पुलकधरैः कलेबरै-
-रुदूहिरे धृतभवदीक्षणोत्सवाः ॥ ५१-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
viniryatastava caraṇāmbujadvayā-
dudañcitaṃ tribhuvanapāvanaṃ rajaḥ |
maharṣayaḥ pulakadharaiḥ kalebarai-
-rudūhire dhṛtabhavadīkṣaṇotsavāḥ || 51-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As Krishna walked through the forest, the sages collected the dust raised by Krishna's tiny lotus feet, smeared their body with it, which has power to purify the three worlds.

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रचारयत्यविरलशाद्वले तले
पशून् विभो भवति समं कुमारकैः ।
अघासुरो न्यरुणदघाय वर्तनीं
भयानकः सपदि शयानकाकृतिः ॥ ५१-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pracārayatyaviralaśādvale tale
paśūn vibho bhavati samaṃ kumārakaiḥ |
aghāsuro nyaruṇadaghāya vartanīṃ
bhayānakaḥ sapadi śayānakākṛtiḥ || 51-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As Krishna and Gopas were grazing the cows in the forest grasslands, suddenly the most terrifying Aghasura demon appeared in the form of a Python and blocked the way.

stanzas.sanskrit:
महाचलप्रतिमतनोर्गुहानिभ-
-प्रसारितप्रथितमुखस्य कानने ।
मुखोदरं विहरणकौतुकाद्गताः
कुमारकाः किमपि विदूरगे त्वयि ॥ ५१-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mahācalapratimatanorguhānibha-
-prasāritaprathitamukhasya kānane |
mukhodaraṃ viharaṇakautukādgatāḥ
kumārakāḥ kimapi vidūrage tvayi || 51-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: When Krishna moved a little away, the Gopas mistook the huge body of the Asura as a mountain and its large spread out mouth as a cave. In their eagerness to explore the forest, they entered the python's open mouth.

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रमादतः प्रविशति पन्नगोदरं
क्वथत्तनौ पशुपकुले सवात्सके ।
विदन्निदं त्वमपि विवेशिथ प्रभो
सुहृज्जनं विशरणमाशु रक्षितुम् ॥ ५१-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pramādataḥ praviśati pannagodaraṃ
kvathattanau paśupakule savātsake |
vidannidaṃ tvamapi viveśitha prabho
suhṛjjanaṃ viśaraṇamāśu rakṣitum || 51-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: When the Gopas reached the snake's belly, they could not withstand the excessive heat and they cried for help. Krishna entered the snake’s mouth to save his helpless friends.

stanzas.sanskrit:
गलोदरे विपुलितवर्ष्मणा त्वया
महोरगे लुठति निरुद्धमारुते ।
द्रुतं भवान् विदलितकण्ठमण्डलो
विमोचयन् पशुप पशून् विनिर्ययौ ॥ ५१-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
galodare vipulitavarṣmaṇā tvayā
mahorage luṭhati niruddhamārute |
drutaṃ bhavān vidalitakaṇṭhamaṇḍalo
vimocayan paśupa paśūn viniryayau || 51-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna kept increasing his size at the throat of the python so much that Aghasura’s breath got choked and cried in pain. Krishna tore the snake's neck killing Aghasura. The Gopas and the cows were saved and came out from the python’s mouth.

stanzas.sanskrit:
क्षणं दिवि त्वदुपगमार्थमास्थितं
महासुरप्रभवमहो महो महत् ।
विनिर्गते त्वयि तु निलीनमञ्जसा
नभःस्थले ननृतुरथो जगुः सुराः ॥ ५१-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kṣaṇaṃ divi tvadupagamārthamāsthitaṃ
mahāsuraprabhavamaho maho mahat |
vinirgate tvayi tu nilīnamañjasā
nabhaḥsthale nanṛturatho jaguḥ surāḥ || 51-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Brilliant light radiated from the body of the snake reaching the sky and then emerged Krishna as Bhagwan came out of the huge snake. Brahma, other Gods and divine sages showered flowers on Krishna.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सविस्मयैः कमलभवादिभिः सुरै-
-रनुद्रुतस्तदनु गतः कुमारकैः ।
दिने पुनस्तरुणदशामुपेयुषि
स्वकैर्भवानतनुत भोजनोत्सवम् ॥ ५१-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
savismayaiḥ kamalabhavādibhiḥ surai-
-ranudrutastadanu gataḥ kumārakaiḥ |
dine punastaruṇadaśāmupeyuṣi
svakairbhavānatanuta bhojanotsavam || 51-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Then Krishna, Balarama and the Gopas enjoyed the lunch picnic by eating the delicious food. Brahma, Devas and other Gods were wonder struck at Krishna seeing the happenings in the forest.

stanzas.sanskrit:
विषाणिकामपि मुरलीं नितम्बके
निवेशयन् कबलधरः कराम्बुजे ।
प्रहासयन् कलवचनैः कुमारकान्
बुभोजिथ त्रिदशगणैर्मुदा नुतः ॥ ५१-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
viṣāṇikāmapi muralīṃ nitambake
niveśayan kabaladharaḥ karāmbuje |
prahāsayan kalavacanaiḥ kumārakān
bubhojitha tridaśagaṇairmudā nutaḥ || 51-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna holding a ball of rice in his hand entertained the Gopas with his humorous talks. Brahma and other Gods watched the above scene and sang joyfully in praise of Krishna.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सुखाशनं त्विह तव गोपमण्डले
मखाशनात्प्रियमिव देवमण्डले ।
इति स्तुतस्त्रिदशवरैर्जगत्पते
मरुत्पुरीनिलय गदात् प्रपाहि माम् ॥ ५१-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sukhāśanaṃ tviha tava gopamaṇḍale
makhāśanātpriyamiva devamaṇḍale |
iti stutastridaśavarairjagatpate
marutpurīnilaya gadāt prapāhi mām || 51-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
The great Gods admired the love shown by Krishna, when He was enjoying the food with the Gopas more than He would have enjoyed the sacrificial yagnas offered by Gods and sang praises.
Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to protect him from his ailments.
